Short human-readable name.

Version of this entity definition, ideally a semantic version such as "1.4.2".
When this entity or version was created.
The Actor responsible for creating this entity or version.
The earlier version this entity revises.

Identifier of the item in its system of record.
Current business state of the item, in the vocabulary of its system of record.
When the item entered the process.
When the item left the process, if it has.

The system, sensor, application, or channel that emitted the Signal.
When the Signal occurred.
Where the raw payload is stored, if it is kept.
Handling classification of the payload.
What was observed, for example "claim_amount" or "handling_time".

When the observation was made.
How the value was derived, for example "document-extraction" or "rule".

Relative business priority.
The period over which the Objective is pursued, for example "FY2027".

Free-text constraints that are not (yet) captured as Policies.
Relative priority.

The situational values themselves.
Handling classification.
When the Context should be considered stale.

Conditions under which the Policy applies.
Consequence of a violation.
Who may override the Policy, and how.

When the Task must be completed.
Display name.

Pointer to the Agent's implementation, model card, or A2A Agent Card.
The team or department the person works in.
How the Orchestrator plans, for example "rule-based", "LLM-planned", "hybrid".
Default handling for failures across the Plans it runs.
Limits on concurrency, cost, or time it must respect.
Whether it blocks before, detects after, or repairs after the fact.
The Actors, Skills, or Work Items it watches.

JSON Schema (or equivalent) for the Skill's inputs.
JSON Schema (or equivalent) for the Skill's outputs.
How to invoke it, for example an MCP tool name, an API endpoint, or a UI automation.
Whether invoking the Skill changes external state, and whether that can be undone.
Typical or maximum latency, for example "< 1s".
Relative cost per invocation.

When the Action ended.
How the Action ended.

Key that makes a retried Action safe to repeat.
The inputs passed to the Skill.
Whether the Action achieved what it set out to.
What the Result is, in words.
Documents, records, or state changes the Result produced.
Certainty between 0 and 1.
What produced the measure.
Whether the value has been calibrated against observed accuracy.
How much the value is expected to move as evidence arrives.
Position on the AL0 to AL4 scale.
What people do at this level.
What Agents may do at this level.
The human oversight this level requires.
Confidence below which an Actor operating at this level must escalate, unless a Policy sets a different floor.
The class of risk this level is suited to.

When the Outcome was measured.
The period the measurement covers.
How long it took for the impact to appear.
How the risk picture changed as a result.
What the Feedback is about.
What went wrong or could be better.
Specific changes proposed.
How urgent the Feedback is.
When the Feedback was given.
Where the memory is held.
How long entries are kept and when they are purged.
